**Helper wrapping secret detection:** `check_secret` (private fn, `src/memory/guard.rs`). It calls `secret_kind` (the public detection fn in the same file), which tests against named-credential regexes in `SECRETS` and a high-entropy token heuristic (`LONG_TOKEN` + `looks_random`).

**Fields `check_secret` is applied to** — all inside `pub(crate) fn check` in `src/memory/guard.rs`:
| Field | Line |
|---|---|
| `text` | 146 |
| `subject` | 156 |
| `key` | 160 |
| each `tag` | 172 |
| each `ref` | 184 |
| `source` | 198 |

**Files and functions involved / affected if the check changes:**

| File | Function / role |
|---|---|
| `src/memory/guard.rs` | `check_secret` — the wrapper; `secret_kind` — the actual detector; `check` — the outer validation entry point that calls `check_secret` for every field above |
| `src/memory/write.rs` | Calls `guard::check` on every `remember` and `forget` write (3 inbound call sites) |
| `src/memory/recall.rs` | 1 call site into guard (uses `secret_kind` or `check_secret` during recall/briefing path) |
| `src/memory/mod.rs` | Imports `guard`; re-exports or routes writes through it (3 inbound call sites) |
| `src/text.rs` | 1 call into guard — uses `secret_kind` directly for text-level credential scanning outside the memory write path |

A change to the credential check logic inside `secret_kind` would propagate to every one of these six fields and to all four calling files. A change only to `check_secret` (e.g. the error message or the refusal policy) would affect the same six fields but not any direct use of `secret_kind` in `src/text.rs` or `src/memory/recall.rs`.
